KNOWN BUG: The dialog's focus trap counts hidden or tabIndex=-1 elements as tabbable (for example the library's own hidden TabPanels inside a Dialog), so Tab moves focus somewhere invisible. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no". - A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no". - Wording does not matter; the behaviour does. === REVIEW FINDINGS === - [blocking] Dialog restores focus to the wrong element when a child uses autoFocus. The Dialog layout effect captures `document.activeElement` after the child's autoFocus has already moved focus into the dialog. On close, focus lands on `body` instead of the Open button. Reproduced: ``, click Open, Escape, then `expect(getByText("Open")).toHaveFocus()` fails with `Received element with focus: `. Fix: capture `previous` before children commit, for example in render or a ref set before the dialog mounts. - [blocking] Focus trap leaks after the focused element is removed. The keydown handler is on the dialog, so when focus falls to `body` (the focused button was removed) Tab is not intercepted and focus moves to the page behind the modal. Reproduced: remove the focused "Remove me" button in an open dialog, then `user.tab()`. `document.activeElement` is ``, outside the dialog.
